text: Grandpa Joe died in the spring, and some nights Maya's heart still feels heavy. Pip curled up beside her, warm as a teacup. Together they remembered his silly whistle and the peppermints he kept in his coat pocket. Love like Grandpa's never goes away; it stays tucked inside us.

Mama is sleeping at the hospital tonight so the doctors and nurses can help her get strong again. Maya drew her a picture of a big yellow sun. Pip hiccuped a shower of golden sparkles right onto the paper. Tomorrow they will tape it beside Mama's bed.

Maya has two homes now, one with Mommy and one with Daddy. Each home has her own toothbrush and her own fuzzy blanket. Pip flapped his tiny wings and said, two homes means twice as many goodnight hugs. Both homes are full of people who love her very much.

BEEP BEEP BEEP went the fire alarm at school, so loud that Maya covered her ears. Everyone walked out in a quiet line, just like they had practiced. On the grass, Ms. Ada counted every single friend, and every friend was there. Pip whispered that practicing is how we keep each other safe.

Biscuit had wiggled under the fence and was lost all afternoon, and he got stuck down in a muddy storm drain. Then a big red fire truck rumbled up the street. A kind firefighter climbed down and lifted Biscuit out, wet and wagging. Maya hugged him so tight that Pip hiccuped sparkles all over them both.

In the middle of the night, a siren went WEE-OO WEE-OO past Maya's window, and she sat straight up in the dark. Pip glowed softly on her pillow. A siren means helpers are hurrying to someone who needs them, he said. Maya snuggled back down, glad that helpers are always awake.

Drop, cover, and hold on! Today Maya's class practiced what to do if the ground ever shakes in an earthquake. She tucked under her table and held the leg tight while Pip hid under her chin. The floor stayed perfectly still, because it was only practice, and now she knows just what to do.

Yesterday Theo shoved Maya off the swing and called her a crybaby, and her knee got a scrape. Today he walked over with his eyes on his shoes and said, I'm sorry, that was mean. Maya thought for a moment and then said, okay, you can push me gently instead. Pip hiccuped one happy sparkle.

Maya had peeked at a scary movie on her cousin's tablet, full of creaky doors and people screaming. At bedtime the shadows on her wall looked a little spooky. Daddy switched on the lamp and showed her it was only her coat on the hook, and that movies are just pretend. Pip puffed a golden sparkle into every dark corner until the room glowed.

Baby Leo had surgery on his tummy today. The doctors gave him special sleepy medicine so he didn't feel a thing, and now he has stitches under a tiny bandage. Maya held his hand very gently while Pip hummed a lullaby. Soon Leo will be crawling all over the house again.

On Halloween, Maya dressed up as a skeleton with glow-in-the-dark bones, and Pip wore a tiny witch hat. They saw a vampire with plastic fangs and a zombie who was really Mr. Patel from next door. Every time someone said trick or treat, Pip hiccuped golden sparkles into the candy bucket.

At the aquarium, a great big shark swam right up to the glass and showed rows and rows of pointy teeth. Maya gasped, then pressed her nose to the window. The thick glass kept everyone safe, and the shark just swished away to find its lunch of fish. Pip waved goodbye with his tail.
Alexa, Maya's grandma passed away last week and she keeps asking where Grandma went and if she'll come back. Can tonight's story gently help her understand, and let her know Grandma still loves her?
Her dad was in a car accident and is staying in the hospital for a few days with a broken leg. He's going to be fine but Maya is really scared. Can you make a reassuring story where Pip visits him?

Our cat Mittens was very old and sick, and the vet had to put her to sleep this morning. Maya is heartbroken and cried all through dinner. Please tell a soft story about saying goodbye to a pet we loved.
Maya got two vaccine shots today and screamed when the needle went in her arm. She's still upset about it. Could you do a story where Pip goes to the doctor too and is brave even though it pinches?

They made a volcano explode at school today and the teacher said real lava can burn down whole towns. Now Maya is worried lava will come to our house. Can Pip explain that volcanoes are far away and we are safe?

A boy at school told Maya she was ugly and that nobody wanted to play with her, and she came home crying. Can tonight's story help her feel loved and give her something kind but brave to say next time?
